issues.description: `construct_zero_state_prep_circuit` has an inconsistent return annotation: the problem statement requires `-> stim.Circuit` and the solution returns a `stim.Circuit`, but the template declares `-> None`. This can mislead students into not returning a circuit and can break any code/tests that expect the returned circuit value.
issues.suggestedFix: In the template, change the signature to `def construct_zero_state_prep_circuit(Hx: npt.NDArray[np.int8], offset: int = 0) -> stim.Circuit:` (and keep the docstring return description consistent).

issues.description: The problem statement specifies `inject(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit: int) -> int`, but the template omits the type annotation on `injection_qubit` (and also omits `: int`), making the interface inconsistent with the specification and potentially confusing for students/tests relying on the documented signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template signature to `def inject(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit: int) -> int:` to match the problem statement.

issues.description: The template docstring for `build_msd_circ` mis-describes the second returned list as indices of 'final X-basis measurements of the distilled state', but the problem statement requires it to be the measurement indices of the destructive X-basis measurements of the 15 tetrahedral-code qubits (in code-qubit order). This naming/description mismatch can cause students to wire the wrong measurement set into error detection/corrections.
issues.suggestedFix: Rewrite the `build_msd_circ` template docstring so the second list is described as: 'measurement indices of the destructive X-basis measurements of the 15 tetrahedral-code qubits (ordered by qubit index/order)', matching the problem statement.
